questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit and driving too fast for conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at safe speeds within the legal limit and with traffic flow.

questions.question: Your reaction time slows after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills get worse. You will have trouble judging distances and the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your ability to drive. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold tablets with alcohol or antihistamines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your vehicle?

options.text: Place them on the floor near the driver's seat.
Secure them to prevent hazards.
Place them on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them to prevent hazards.
questions.explanation: Loose objects can hit and injure people during a sudden stop or crash. Objects on the floor can roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal your intention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before making any move to the left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves. Slow down appropriately.

questions.question: If railroad crossing gates are lowered with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings with warning signs, lights, or flaggers. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt than on pavement. You must slow down. Stopping takes much longer and skidding is easier when turning.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time and gets you there faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before you proceed.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to road conditions. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or switch drivers.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or switch drivers.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can each rest.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors well.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of one, the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive under the influence of medication that impairs your driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if it is prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has stopped in your lane with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights turn off. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus uses flashing lights and its stop arm, you must not move until the lights and stop arm are turned off. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: A driver sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should the driver do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians in a crosswalk cross the street. Wait until the intersection is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: You are approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left.
Continue driving when you think most children are done exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm extended and lights flashing. Stay stopped until the stop arm is retracted and the lights turn off.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass many cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and more safely.
You will increase your chances of a collision.
You will help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a collision goes up.

questions.question: What is the best way to change from one lane to another?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Change lanes only when necessary. Every lane change increases your risk of an accident.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fight the feeling.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the nearest rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest and can make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If you see animals standing near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so there may be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move into the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, make sure other drivers can see it. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your emergency flashers to show other drivers you are having trouble.
